doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Recording 'A Dog' with Al Foster and Branford
summary: Playing a track, she explains the barking call and that Al Foster urged her to hire Branford to play alto.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I wanted to play just a bit of one of your tunes here. And maybe you can tell me—
Now, I’m curious about those thick horn harmonies, how you got that. Because you only had two horns, but are you playing that kind of with them or something?
Well that was “A Dog,” written for my dog, my little FiFi. Tujai FiFi Tee Tai Tae was his whole name but his nickname was FiFi.
What was his full name again?

Tujai FiFi Te Tai Tae. So it was a little Yorkie dog. Crazy. A very crazy Yorkie dog. He would, we had loft beds that were about up to the top of the curtain there. And if you were chopping carrots, that was his favorite thing to eat, raw carrots, he’d jump right off the loft. This little tiny dog. I mean a very crazy dog. And the little call at the beginning of the recording, that works for ninety percent of any Yorkies. If you go down the street in New York and see a Yorkie and you want it to turn around and come to you, you do that, in that pitch. They come. I’ve done it. There’s some mad owners too. That was Branford barking.
Oh it was Branford? Well you asked him to do a couple different things then. He was on alto on that thing, right? “And you have to bark—”

You know I didn’t do that, no that was Al Foster. Because Al, you know I called Al, I wanted him to be the drummer and there was a tenor — I can’t remember who I had, I just know I wanted alto. And you know he said, “Well why don’t you get Branford?” I said, “Well he’s like tenor.” Al says, “No, no, no, I’ve seen, he has an alto, I’ve seen it, call him.”

So he kept telling me that and finally I did. I didn’t know Branford then so I took his word for it, and he did, he didn’t have, I remember he didn’t have the neck strap, so he was like playing with no neck strap.
